newsitem.title: GERMANY: German govt denies report of 4.15 pct defict ratio.
newsitem.headline: German govt denies report of 4.15 pct defict ratio.

text.p: A German government spokesman on Saturday denied a magazine report that the chancellor's office expects that Germany's deficit could climb well beyond Maastricht Treaty target levels this year.

According to a report to appear in this week's edition of Spiegel magazine, internal calculations made by Chancellor Helmut Kohl's office show a budget deficit of up to 4.15 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).

Such a figure is well beyond the expectations of most private economists and the three percent target level mandated by the Maastricht Treaty for countries hoping to join European monetary union (EMU).
A preview of the magazine article was provided to the media before its official publication.
Most private economists expect a deficit ratio this year of slightly over three percent. It stood at 3.8 percent in 1996.

Despite signs that Germany will have difficulty trimming its budget deficit in time to qualify for EMU, Finance Minister Theo Waigel has maintained that Bonn will cut the deficit to 2.9 percent of GDP this year.
